overall: Atlanta is in the early hours of July 6 with a current temperature of 73.4°F and a running daily max of just 75.2°F, well below where the day should peak. Conditions are humid (dewpoint ~70°F), nearly calm winds, and partly cloudy skies — a setup typical of a warm, storm-threatened summer day. The key story for today is the 60% chance of afternoon thunderstorms (Flash Flood Warnings still active from overnight convection), which could cap or cut short the afternoon warm-up.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance is notably split: GFS is a warm outlier at 93.4°F while ECMWF (88.4°F), HRRR (87.1°F), and NBM (87.3°F) cluster tightly in the 87-88°F range — a 5-6°F spread that signals real uncertainty. The NWS narrative reflects this tension, headlining a high 'near 91°F' but explicitly noting temperatures 'falling to around 87°F in the afternoon' once storms arrive, suggesting storm timing relative to peak heating is the critical variable.
max_temp_prediction: The META model (most reliable fusion) strongly favors the 90-91°F bucket at 50.8%, consistent with the NWS headline high. However, the active market uses ODD buckets, where 89-90°F leads at only 17.3% — a flat, uncertain distribution flagged as Tier 4/no-trade by the ensemble. If afternoon storms arrive before the temperature peak (~2 PM local), the high could be suppressed into the 87-89°F range consistent with ECMWF/HRRR/NBM; if storms are delayed or the pre-storm warm-up runs longer, 90-91°F is achievable. Best estimate is near 90°F with moderate confidence, but storm timing introduces meaningful downside risk toward 88-89°F.
